source.title: Sharpness Minimization Algorithms Do Not Only Minimize Sharpness To Achieve Better Generalization
source.authors: Kai-Yue Wen; Zhiyuan Li; Tengyu Ma

record.tranche_reason: The study reports that the relation between trace-Hessian sharpness and generalization changes with architecture, and that sharpness minimization can fail to generalize in some settings. Its experiments use synthetic parity data and do not test the claim versions' specified settings or V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure.
record.gate_note: Empirical results use 1-SAM on synthetic parity data, not natural labels. The text gives qualitative figure descriptions but no test-error numbers for these experiments; cited prior work is not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether minimizing unscaled trace-Hessian sharpness guarantees generalization on synthetic tasks. V7 concerns magnitude-aware weight perturbations and their correlation with generalization gaps; this study neither measures that quantity nor compares its ranking with norm- and margin-based measures. Its results do not test any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that whether minimal trace-Hessian sharpness implies generalization depends on architecture and data distribution, and that SAM can generalize even when poorly generalizing global sharpness minimizers exist. They therefore argue that mechanisms beyond minimizing this sharpness measure contribute to SAM's generalization benefits.
record.recipe_differences: Uses 1-SAM and synthetic parity or uniform-ball tasks with two-layer networks; it does not test the claim versions' original natural-data settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with architecture, including bias and simplified normalization, and with the tested data distribution. The biased ReLU network with logistic loss starts to degenerate after 2000 epochs; with mean squared error, the corresponding result starts after 4000 epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: On synthetic parity data, SAM produces generalizing solutions without bias or with simplified normalization, but biased ReLU and Softplus models can generalize worse than weight-decay baselines despite lower trace-Hessian sharpness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generalization associated with minimizing unscaled trace-Hessian sharpness depends on architecture and training conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: On the uniform-ball regression task, the SAM-trained network without bias generalizes substantially better than the network with bias.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding first-layer bias can change the generalization of solutions found by trace-Hessian sharpness minimization.

fits_no_version.finding: For biased and simplified-LayerNorm networks on parity data, the theory constructs equally minimal trace-Hessian solutions with zero generalization error and with error max{1 − n/2^d, 0}.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Minimal unscaled trace-Hessian sharpness alone does not determine generalization, even among interpolating solutions of the same architecture.

record.problems: Experiments cover a small subset of architectures and use synthetic distributions. Empirical outcomes are described qualitatively in figure-referenced text without numerical test-error values or uncertainty estimates. The authors note that their analysis assumes 1-SAM finds a valid global sharpness minimizer, while prior proofs establish only a local tendency to decrease sharpness.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported result meeting the row criteria was omitted. Table 2 lists hyperparameters by figure but does not report additional outcomes.

untested.parts: No comparison of fixed random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and chance performance on held-out random labels.
No width sweep beyond the width needed to interpolate; experimental width is fixed at 500.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison or test of learned local connectivity.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison under limited or broader tuning.
No controlled batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets; optimizer, regularization, and training recipes differ between SAM and the baseline.

No magnitude-aware perturbation measure, correlation ranking of generalization gaps within a convolutional family, or comparison against norm- and margin-based measures. Counterexamples for unscaled Hessian trace do not test this version.
No removal of highly memorized examples followed by retraining and comparison with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: The cannot_determine states concern the listed claim versions, not whether the study reports its own effects. The supplied text supports the qualitative empirical outcomes, but contains no readable numerical test-error curves. Section 4 and Section 5 headings swap 'former' and 'latter'; their substantive text, Table 1, and figure captions establish the intended outcomes. Additional logistic-loss outcomes in Figures 8 and 10 also fit no listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting fixed random labels with generalizing on natural labels.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD.
Does not vary batch size or assess large-batch generalization.
Measures trace of the Hessian rather than magnitude-aware sharpness; does not compare the specified measures within one convolutional family.
Does not remove influential memorized examples and retrain.

rows.subject: 2-layer MLP with ReLU activation without bias
rows.operation_detail: Trained with 1-SAM on Pxor; the text compares its generalization with a baseline trained using gradient descent with weight decay.
rows.baseline: Baseline reaches perfect generalization; its sharpness is higher than the 1-SAM minimum.
rows.value: 1-SAM interpolates the training set and reaches a flat minimum that generalizes perfectly.
rows.note: The text describes the result qualitatively; no test-error number is supplied.
rows.check: Perfect generalization and low trace-Hessian sharpness are reported, but neither establishes V7's magnitude-aware correlation. No random-label comparison tests V1.

rows.subject: 2-layer MLP with simplified BN

conditions.value: Complete Training Set Condition not enforced

rows.value: SAM finds a flat minimum that generalizes well; inspected neurons approximately extract features ±x[1] ± x[2].
rows.note: Qualitative result; no test-error number is supplied.
rows.check: Generalization and feature extraction under simplified BatchNorm do not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: 2-layer MLP with ReLU activation with Bias
rows.operation_detail: Trained with 1-SAM and compared with full-batch gradient descent with weight decay.
rows.baseline: Baseline generalizes better; 1-SAM reaches a flatter minimum.
rows.value: 1-SAM model fails to generalize, and generalization performance starts to degenerate after 4000 epochs.
rows.note: The text describes the comparison qualitatively; no test-error number is supplied.
rows.check: The flatter SAM solution generalizes worse than the weight-decay baseline, but this is not a reversal of V7's magnitude-aware correlation. The reported outcome concerns a different sharpness measure.

rows.subject: 2-layer ReLU network with simplified LayerNorm
rows.operation_detail: Trained with 1-SAM; one condition restricts first-layer weight and bias norms to 10.

conditions.value: standard training or projected training with first-layer weight and bias norms restricted to 10

rows.value: In both conditions, models almost perfectly generalize; the text says SAM improves generalization till perfect generalization.
rows.note: Qualitative result; no test-error number is supplied.
rows.check: Near-perfect generalization under simplified LayerNorm does not test a listed version. Standard and projected training should be separate rows because they are distinct conditions.

rows.subject: 2-layer MLP with Softplus activation with bias
rows.operation_detail: Trained with 1-SAM and compared with gradient descent with weight decay.
rows.value: Converged models found by SAM fail to generalize.
rows.note: The text reports a qualitative result; no test-error number is supplied.
rows.check: SAM's failure to generalize with biased Softplus networks does not establish a reversal of any listed version.

rows.subject: 2-layer MLP with ReLU activation with Bias
rows.operation_detail: Trained with 1-SAM and compared with gradient descent with weight decay using logistic loss with label smoothing.
rows.baseline: Baseline generalizes better; 1-SAM reaches a flatter minimum.
rows.value: 1-SAM model generalizes much worse and starts to degenerate after 2000 epochs.
rows.note: The text describes the result qualitatively; no test-error number is supplied.
rows.check: The logistic-loss comparison shows lower trace-Hessian sharpness with worse generalization, not a reversal of V7's magnitude-aware measure.

rows.subject: 2-layer MLP without bias
rows.operation_detail: Trained with 1-SAM on a uniform ball distribution.
rows.measure: Generalization performance of the flattest minimizer
rows.baseline: Compared with the 2-layer MLP with bias in the same experiment.

rows.note: Qualitative comparison; no test-error number is supplied.
